selected.text: Consider how many souls arose after Christ to extinguish the divine lamp, and even the Roman Emperor, who was the greatest philosopher, arose with utmost might to oppose and wrote a book in refutation of Christ, publishing it throughout his realm and causing some to turn away from Christ. Yet ultimately the power of the Word of God prevailed over the Roman Empire and the light of the divine Covenant dispelled the darkness of doubts cast by those philosophers and kings.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls how many, even the Roman Emperor, failed to extinguish the lamp lit by Christ.

selected.text: The verses are like unto water; even as water giveth life to bodies, as ye behold, even so do the verses give life unto spirits, and cause to grow from the soil of divine knowledge trees of exalted glory. Say: At times they appear according to the nature of fire, whereby are set ablaze the hearts of them that have turned towards God, the Mighty, the Beloved. And at times thou findest them according to the nature of water, for by them liveth all that was and all that shall be.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh teaches that the verses give life to spirits as water gives life to bodies.

selected.text: Through its potency whatsoever is recorded in Thy holy Scriptures and sacred Books hath been made manifest and Thy messengers and Thy chosen ones have raised their Call, so that all men may be infused with the capacity to attain Thy presence, to direct their steps toward the ocean of Thy nearness, to present themselves before the seat of Thy throne and to give ear unto Thy wondrous Voice, calling aloud from the Dayspring of Thine invisible Essence and from the Dawning-Place of Thine exalted Being.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: If ye turn not your eyes toward the words of God, God will soon raise up a people who will look upon them with Mine eyes, who will read My verses and weep for what hath befallen My Beauty, the Stranger, the Imprisoned, the Distressed. We have worlds beyond worlds, creation beyond creation, remembrance beyond remembrance, command beyond command, books beyond books, and sanctified, self-subsisting pages. We nurture every world by Our command and favor, for I am the Powerful over what I will, the Mighty, the Beloved.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warns that if people turn not to His words, God will raise up others who will read them and weep.

selected.text: Therefore, all these before mentioned bonds of love are subjected to cessation and a day may come when that love will cease to exist, will vanish, but our love is indissolvable, is eternal, is everlasting for the bonds which have bound this love are absolutely contingent upon the love of God and the Bounty of the Word of God is eternal. If the forces of all the world contend they could not find the least access or entrance into this bond of love. … And now my purpose is to send you in this wise, supported by this bond to America for the greatest power in the realm of existence is the Word God and no power can withstand it
selected.reason: A reported talk contrasts the bonds of love that pass away with the love born of the Word, which endures.

selected.text: The Word, in its primary essence, is the water of life for the dead of the world and the hand of power for the salvation of nations. Through a single exalted word, it draws man from the darkness of idle fancies to the light of certitude, and from the deep pit to the lofty palace.
selected.reason: The Word in its primary essence is called the water of life for the dead and the hand of power for the nations.

selected.text: Now people demand proof from one who makes a claim. What proof could be greater than that God should cause someone to appear in Persia speaking in the language of the Qur'an, such that if all the peoples of the earth were to gather together, they could not understand a single word of these utterances, let alone produce their like? Now, setting aside what has already been revealed, the Surih that has been revealed in this very leaf suffices as proof for all the peoples of the earth. If the entire Qur'an were but a single surih, could anyone say it is not proof? God forbid! Rather, this surih in its proving power equals the decree of the Qur'an and the miracle of all the Prophets and Successors, could they but comprehend.
selected.reason: The Báb asks what proof could be greater than one appearing in Persia and speaking in the language of the Qur’an.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No authorized paragraph; supplied fragments differ from the provisional rendering.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH04507 version 7a59a8617b21c0cb3b4501866330666edf481992f147a724d59de19a0048c22d, metadata Authorized empty. The supplied This is a Book which the All-Merciful hath sent down agrees with the opening of paragraph2, but the ellipsis then jumps to a closing sentence on fragrance and the Most Exalted Pen that the provisional paragraphs2-3 render differently, and it omits the address to Ashraf and his poem in praise of God. Omit as an elided fragment; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph3; supplied wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB10953 version 99c3be7e07b713b137145426198b35ad42770115bda331907734301ad3fce77a paragraph3, metadata Y3, whose translations include TAB.690-692. The authorized wording reads the power of the Word of God penetrateth all things and the assistance of the divine Kingdom is, within a sentence on intention, confirmation and action in the cause of peace; the supplied the power of the Word of God is penetrative and the existence of the divine Kingdom is uninterrupted is the older Tablets of Abdul-Baha rendering. Omit; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph3; supplied wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH03840 version 470bf9800ffcd6b113de7643c7e1b1d2eba05b173d2ed62a49231781187a1e7a paragraph3, metadata Y3, cited as The Advent of Divine Justice 75-76. The authorized wording addressed to the people of Baha reads Beware lest anything withhold you from observing the things prescribed unto you by the Most Exalted Pen; the supplied that which ye have been commanded by the Most Exalted Pen when it moved across the Tablet is a different rendering. Omit; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference TB.257 not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Whole supplied extract read, cited as TB.257. No candidate record was supplied, and a search of the English corpus found related Tablets on the human tree and its fruits (BH09151, BH02956, BH00558) but none containing this wording. The ellipsis after a goodly utterance is preserved. Retain the supplied wording and unmatched status; no context restored and no authority asserted.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Supplied wording cited as Gleanings CXXIX; catalogue paragraph4 lies outside the authorized range Y22 and is a different rendering.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH00144 version f3247e62cc0d4a3e422902fe64036ae5a80ae7a8a773c01a9ddc59565c8c03e4 paragraph4, metadata Y22, whose translations include GWB#129x. The provisional paragraph4 reads Were all who are in the heavens and earth to be given but a drop thereof, they would find themselves enriched; the supplied A dewdrop out of this ocean would, if shed upon all that are in the heavens and on the earth, suffice to enrich them is the Gleanings wording, which could not be checked against the official page in this review. Retain conservatively with approximate status; no authority transferred to the catalogue paragraph.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Authorized prayer paragraph1, with an ellipsis preserved.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH09162 version 6a777a63cb5612257bb60adc253d780b8246bcade31cec3b31b163775091c2a5 paragraph1, metadata Y, cited as Prayers and Meditations X. The supplied O Thou ... the words of Whose mouth are as the waters of life unto all who are in heaven and on earth agrees exactly with the opening and close of the authorized invocation; the ellipsis omits the intervening attributes of God's face, presence, nearness, name and voice. Include for the authorized words and preserve approximate status.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Authorized paragraph18 wording, with one verb tense difference preserved.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH00657 version 2db0cf17e9fe9c9d23e70f4d8fe288a4d3c4d4ae6bbb2015823ac423dd347974 paragraph18, metadata Y14-23, cited as Gleanings CXXI. The authorized sentence reads The Tongue of God testifieth to the truth of My words, through Mine own Word that speaketh the truth, and embraceth and comprehendeth all things; the supplied wording agrees except testified for testifieth. Include conservatively for the authorized sentence without adopting the variant, and preserve approximate status.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Different rendering of authorized paragraph5; supplied wording not authorized.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared BH02443 version 519b5fd2eabcd2c8599450e04be2ba3d305198605f537d56fe15fd3dc9f3812f paragraph5, metadata Y, cited as Tablets of Baha'u'llah. The authorized wording reads We have encompassed the world through Our Most Exalted Word. God shall, through it, soon conquer the hearts of all who dwell on earth, and that exact wording is already selected as a mandatory linked passage; the supplied through the potency of the Most Sublime Word and the time is approaching when God will have subdued is a different rendering. Omit; no authority transferred.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: Candidate paragraph4 is authorized but does not contain the supplied wording.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: Compared AB00022 version bc7dd28eb8ccce80f8d1eab2f07dd494777575c5009bcc174a632ad7859801fd paragraph4, metadata Y. The authorized paragraph ends Its penetrative power is the Word of God, which only echoes the theme. The supplied the power of the Word of God is penetrative and the existence of the divine Kingdom is uninterrupted, cited as TAB.691, repeats the imported wording reviewed for AB10953 paragraph3, whose translations list TAB.690-692. Omit as a mismatched duplicate; no authority transferred.
